title: Pakistan School Roof Collapse Kills 33 Children and Teacher in Peshawar
text:
At least 33 children and a teacher were killed when a school roof collapsed in Peshawar, Pakistan, during morning classes. The owner has been arrested as authorities investigate.
At least 33 children and their female teacher were killed at the Al Khair Education Center in Peshawar, Pakistan, on Thursday when the roof of a building collapsed during morning classes. The incident occurred in a poor district of Peshawar, the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province near the Afghan border. Local hospitals said they were treating about 50 injured people, including three children in critical condition.
Collapse During Morning Classes
According to local officials, the roof from a higher floor collapsed and brought two stories of the school building down, crushing the students and teacher beneath. The Al Khair Education Center was a three-story building with about 1,200 students. Peshawar police chief Saeed Ahmed said 110 students were attending lessons in three classrooms when the disaster struck. Most of the students are 13 or younger, and some are only six years old.
A teacher from another school who rushed to the scene told the BBC that he personally pulled out six children with his own hands. He said that most of them were alive and talking, but later it was found that they had passed away.
Arrest and Negligence Allegations
Ahmed said the owner of the school, Mohammad Khan, has been arrested. Khan denied accusations of negligence, saying heavy rains caused the roof to become weak enough to collapse. Reuters quoted distraught relatives of the dead and injured accusing school officials of ignoring their concerns about poor maintenance and shoddy construction. The school is one of many low-cost private institutions that serve Pakistan's poorest residents, as the government spends very little on public education, and even less on oversight for private academies. A similar roof collapse catastrophe in Lahore in June killed 14 children.
Police chief Ahmed pledged a thorough investigation into possible violation of building codes in the incident. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa governor Faisal Karim Kundi ordered a safety audit of all schools, to identify potential risks and ensure that immediate corrective measures are taken wherever necessary.
Government Response and Public Outcry
The Al Khair center is located in a poor district of Peshawar, the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa near the Afghan border, a province that was under a state of emergency on Monday by President Shehbaz Sharif due to cross-border attacks by Islamist terrorists. An angry Peshawar resident who said his two nephews were killed in the roof collapse demanded that authorities make an example of those responsible, a lesson for all, so that no one dares open a school just to make money without providing facilities. The tragedy has highlighted the lack of oversight in Pakistan's private education sector, where low-cost institutions often operate without adequate safety checks.
